title: L5 · Tissues
subtitle: Matrix, cell junctions, epithelium, connective tissue

lines.text: A tissue is a group of similar cells. Its study is histology.
**Epithelial** tissue covers.
**Connective** tissue supports.
**Muscle** moves. **Nervous** tissue controls.
Every tissue is cells plus matrix.
The matrix is **ground substance** plus fibers.
Fibroblasts make the fibers.
**Collagen** is the strongest fiber.
**Elastic** fibers stretch and recoil.
**Reticular** fibers are thin branched networks that support organs.
Epithelium covers and lines every free surface. It also forms glands.
It is highly **cellular**, with very little matrix.
It is highly **mitotic**. It replaces itself quickly.
It is **avascular**. It has no blood supply of its own.
It has an **apical** surface on top and a basal surface below.
**Tight junctions** fuse cells into a seal. Nothing leaks between them.
**Gap junctions** are protein tubes called connexons. They let cells communicate, like in the heart.
**Desmosomes** are spot welds. They resist stress in the heart and epidermis.
**Hemidesmosomes** anchor the epithelium to the basement membrane below.
Epithelium has a first name and a last name.
The first name is layers. **Simple** is one layer. **Stratified** is two or more.
The last name is shape.
**Squamous** is flat. **Cuboidal** is cube. **Columnar** is column.
**Simple squamous** is thin for fast diffusion. Air sacs and capillaries.
**Simple cuboidal** secretes and absorbs. Kidney tubules.
**Simple columnar** lines the digestive tract, stomach to rectum.
Its goblet cells make mucus.
**Pseudostratified** columnar is really one layer.
Its nuclei sit at different heights, so it looks layered.
It has goblet cells and **cilia**.
It lines the **trachea**.
Stratified squamous protects.
**Keratinized** is dry and waterproof. It forms the outer epidermis.
**Non-keratinized** is wet. It lines the mouth.
Stratified cuboidal and columnar are rare. They line some ducts.
**Transitional** is the only epithelium that stretches. It lines the bladder.
Connective tissue is almost the opposite of epithelium.
Few cells. Lots of **matrix**. Low turnover. Very **vascular**.
All adult connective tissue comes from **mesenchyme**.
Wharton's jelly keeps the umbilical cord open.
Adult connective tissue has four kinds: proper, cartilage, blood and bone.
Dense tissue has more fibers and less ground substance.
**Dense regular** has parallel collagen. It is strong in one direction. Tendons and ligaments.
**Dense irregular** has collagen in all directions. It is strong every way. The dermis.
**Elastic** tissue stretches. Vocal cords, lungs and large arteries.
Loose tissue has fewer fibers and more ground substance.
**Areolar** has all three fibers. It's the body's packing material.
**Adipose** is fat. PIES: protects, insulates, energy storage.
**Reticular** tissue supports soft organs like lymph nodes.
Cartilage has no blood and no nerves. Its cells are chondrocytes.
**Hyaline** is the most common. Rib cartilage, joint surfaces, tracheal rings.
**Elastic cartilage** bends. The ear and the epiglottis.
**Fibrocartilage** resists compression. Discs, menisci and the pubic symphysis.
Blood is the only liquid connective tissue.
Its matrix is **plasma**. Its fibers are dissolved clotting proteins.
Bone has a solid matrix.
Its ground substance is **hydroxyapatite**, a calcium salt.
Its fibers are **osteoid**, mostly collagen.
